holidays.name: International Carrot Day
holidays.description: A crunchy salute to the humble orange root. Fans celebrate by snacking on carrots, baking carrot cake, and sneaking the veggie into every course of the meal.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a favorite among gardeners, home cooks, and vegetable lovers.
holidays.funFact: Carrots were not always orange. Early cultivated varieties were often purple or yellow, and the orange kind became popular in Europe in the 1600s.

holidays.name: World Rat Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate rats as clever, social, affectionate animals. Pet rat owners and animal lovers use it to challenge the creature's bad reputation.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial observance with unclear origins. Rat fanciers and animal welfare supporters have helped keep it going.
holidays.funFact: Rats laugh in ultrasonic chirps when they are tickled or play-wrestling. Humans can't hear it without special equipment.

holidays.name: National Hug a Newsperson Day
holidays.description: A day to thank the reporters, editors, photographers, and broadcasters who keep communities informed. Give a journalist a hug, or at least a warm thank-you.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It encourages people to appreciate the people behind the headlines.
holidays.funFact: The word "scoop" for an exclusive story was popular in newsrooms by the late 1800s. It comes from the idea of scooping up a story before competitors can.
